entries.source: Geschichte der Grafen von Wertheim von den ältesten bis zu ihrem Erlöschen im Mannsstamme im Jahre 1556, Nr. LXXII. , S. 103, LXXII.

Die Gebrüder Rudolf und Rudolf Grafen von Wert heim kaufen vom Fuldaer Abt Heinrich das Dorf Cellingen. 1327. März 16.

Nos Henricus dei gratia Fuldensis ecclcsie Abbas. Ad universorum tam presentium quam futurorum deducimus no- titiam publice in bis scriptis, quod honorabilibus ac nobilibus viris Rudolfo de Wertheim, canonico majoris ecclesie Herbip., et Rudolfo Comiti de Wertheim fratribus pro se et suis he- redibus ementibus et recipientibus villam nostram Oellingen cum omnibus pertinentiis nobis et nostre ecclesie in ipsa villa competentibus, quesitis et inquirendis, herbergis nostris duntaxat exceptis, quas nobis et nostris successoribus reser vantes, de consensu unanimi, voluntario et expresso dilec- torum in Christo filiorum Theodorici decani totiusque con- ventus ecclesie mee pref. maturo consilio, solemnique trac- tatu cum eisdem super hoc diligentius prehabitis, vendidimus et tradidimus pro pretio quingentarum libr. hall. nobis pre- dictos emptores in parata et numerata pecunia soluto ac in evidentes nostras et ecclesie nostre utilitates exposito et converso nee non justo venditionis titulo damus et Iradimus libere per presentes, hoc tamen moderaminc addito, quod nobis et successoribus nostris ex specialis favoris ipsorum emptorum indultu predict. villam cum juribus suis et perti nentiis, ut prescribitur, apud diet. Rudolfum canonicum prin- cipaliter, si pro tempore vixerit, ac ipso nоn existente apud prelib. Rudolfum Comitem ipsius fratrem vel suos heredes pro antedicto pretio D libr. hall. dativorum anno quocunque voluerint reemendi libera sit facultas, dummodo XIV diebus festum cathedre s. Petri precedentibus immediate aut sequen- tibus per nos reemptio ipsa fiat, qua reemptione sic facta dicta villa cum omnibus juribus et pertinentiis, quibus nobis pertinere noscebat, ad nos et nostram eccl. sine impedimento quolibet libere revolvetur nee ipsam villam a persona seu personis quavis alia vel aliis quam per nos ipsos et nostram eccles. reemi ullatenus admittemus. Act. et dat. an. domini MCCCXXVII, feria II. post Dominic., qua cantatur Oculi. 78 Lxxln. Vereinigung zwischen Konrad Herrn zu Weinsperg und dessen ehelicher Wirthin Frau Luckard, geb. v. Breuberg, und ihrem Schwager Graf Rudolph von Wertheim und dessen Hausfrau Else, geb. von Breuberg, wie es künftig mit ersterer Erb schaft und besonders mit der Herrschaft Breuberg gehalten werde solle. 1327. April 20. Wir Chunrad herre tzu Winsperch vnd wir frowe Luckardt sin eliche wirtin, geborn von Bruberch veriehen offenlich an disem brif vnd tun chunt allen di in sehen lesen oder horent lesen, das wir vnd de edel mann Greue Rudolf von Wertheim vnser swager vnd frowe Else sin elich frowe geborn von Bruberch vnser swester liplich vnd fruntlich mit wol bedachtem mut mit gutem willen vnd rat vnser frunde vereint und verrihte sin vmb alle gut di vns frowen Elsen vnd frowen Lugkard vorgenant von vnserm vater vnd muter an geuallen sint oder noch an geuallen möchte vnd mit rat diser erbern lute di hernach geschriben sint, hr n Chunrad Schenken herren tzu Ertpach, hrn. Rabens von Helmstat vnd hrn Arnold von Rosenberch ritter, di wir bedersit vmb alle sache bruche oder vfluffe die tzwischen vns vnsern Ampt- luten burchmannen vnsern dinern oder andern unsern luten an demselben erbe vnd guten, swi si genant sint, geschehen mochten, einmuticlich daruff erkorn vnd erwelt haben tzu schidluten, vnd sin also gerichtet als hernach geschriben stet: Were das vnsere libe swester frowe Else vorgenant von Wertheim abe ginge an lip Erben, das Got wende, so sol vnser vorgnanter swager Greue Rudolf von Wertheim, alle di gut vnd erbe, gesucht vnd vngesucht, swi si genant sint, di vnser vorgnant swester frowe Elsen an geuallen waren von vater vnd von muter, bi iren leben, geruclichen haben vnd nizzen di wil er lebt, in allem rechte als vor vnd nach sime tode sullen diselben gut vallen alle an vns vorgnante frowen Luckard vnd vnser lip erben, in allem rechten als sie vnser vorgnant swester bis an irn tode gehabt hat. Wir veriehen auch, were das wir des vorgnanten erbes, es were burge, stet, dörflVr. wiler, vogtei, kirchensatze, manlehen, gulte, nutze, holtz, wasser weide, oder swi es gnant sie, 79 gesucht oder vngesucht, das zu dejn erbe gehört, lützel oder vil verchouffen wolten, das sullen wir vnserm swager Greuen Rudolf vnd vnser swester frowen Elsen, den vor- gnanten oder derselben frowen Elsen Iip erben, ob sie nicht were, tzwen monad vor chuntlich bieten, on alle geuerde, ob si es chouffen wöllen vnd sullen, in den vorgnanten Greue Rudolf frowen Elsen, oder ir lip erben, die gulte nicht hoher geben, danne als hernach geschriben stet, iglich pfund heller geltes, vmb tzehen pfund heller, ein malter korn geltes vmb vir pfund heller, ein malter habern geltes vmb zwei pfund heller vnd ein fuder win geltes nach der gewonheit der gegend, da der win wehset, on alle geuerde. Es ist auch mer geret, were, das wir der vorgnant Chunrad Herre tzu Winsperch vnd wir frowe Luckard sin elich wirtin oder vnser lip erben des vorgeschriben erbes burge, stet, dörf- fer, wiler, vogtei, kirchensetze, manlehen, holtz, wasser, weide, gesucht vnd vngesucht, swi es gnant ist des dartzu gehort, dem vorgenants vnserm swager, Greuen Rudolf frowen Elsen siner elichen wirtin vnd derselben frowen lip erben, chunt- lichen büten, so ungitlich, das gut das wir danne verchouf- fen wöllen, vnd es tzu hohe schatzten, also das si duhte, das es tzu ture were, oder mit geuerde, das sollen wir den vor geschriben drien, hrn. Chunrad dem Schencken, hrn. Raben von Helmstat, vnd hrn. Arnold von Rosenberch chunt tun vnd fur legen, diselben sullen das selbe gut swi es genant si als vorgeschriben stet, schatzen uf ir eide vnd swi si das richten tzwischen vns, das sullen wir bedersit stet halten, vf vnsere eide, den wir Chunrad von Winsperch egnant vnd vnser egnant swager Greue Rudolf darvmb zu den heilgen haben getan. Wir veriehen auch mer, were das vnser vorgnant swager Greue Rudolf frowe Else, sin elich frowe vnser swester vnd derselben lip erben, des vorge schriben erbes ihres lützel oder vil vmb vns Chunrad von Winsperch, oder vmb vns frowen Luckard egnant oder vn ser lip erben kouften, das si die vorgenanten dasselbe gelt, das vmb den kouf geburt zu geben, geben sullen tzu den tzilen als hernach geschriben ist, 1 tusent pfund heller tzu iglichen virtels jars minnere oder mere, darnach sich der kouf geburt, vnd nach gelicher antzal, der tzince vnd des geltes. Es ist auch geret, were, das vnser vorgnant swager vnd swester, Greue Rudolf, vnd frowe Else vnd derselben vnserer swester lip erben in den tzwen monaden als wir Chunrad vnd wir frowe Luckard von Winsperch oder vnsrer 80 frowen Luckard lip erben vorgnant den kouf, den wir in vor chuntlich geboten haben, sich mit vns nicht verenten vmb denselben kouf swi der genant si, so haben wir vor genant Chunrad vnd frowe Luckard von Winsperch, vnd unsrer frowen Luckard lip erben, kraft vnd macht denselben kouf vnd dasselbe gut swi des genant si tzu verkouffen vnd tzu verendern anderswa nach vnsrm willen, swi wir mugen vnd sal vns daran die egenanter vnser swager vnd vnser swester noch ir lip erben nicht irren mit cheinerlei sache weder mit worten oder werken, das vns tzu schaden mochte chomen. Wir veriehen auch mere, were das chein vflouffe wurde tzwischen vnser beder amptluten, burchmannen, di- nern oder andern vnsern luten, di tzu dem vorgeschriben erbe gehören, das wir dartzu nihts tun sullen, wanne wir bedersit daruber erkorn haben vnd genomen, dise erbern lute, hrn. Chunrad Schenken von Ertpach den vorgenant, hrn. Starkrad vnd hrn. Wortwin von Reibach, ritter, burch- manne tzu Bruberch, di solche hruche vnd vfluffe wenden vnd rihten sullen, in dem nehsten monad als in das chunt wirt getan, vnd were das derselbe dri das niht gerihten möchten in demselben monade, so sullen si tzu in nemen, die tzwen vorgeschriben ritter hrn. Raben von Helmstat vnd hrn. Arnold von Rosenberch, di sullen es danne mit einander rihten, nach minne oder nach rehte, swah das vf- loufs wurde in eime monade darnach allernehstc on allegeuerde, vnd swa der vorgenannten drier ritter di vber solche brache vnd vflouffe erkorn wurden vnd genomen ir zwene tun vilen, den sol auch der dritte volgen on widerrede. Were auch das derselben drier einer ab ginge, so sullen die an dern tzwen einen andern kisen vnd nemen an desselben stat, als gemeinen in eime monad nehste darnach. Were aber das hr. Chunrad der vorgenant Schenke ab ginge, das got wende, so sullen di tzwen vorgenant ritter hr. Raben von Helmstat vnd hr. Arnold von Rosenberch ein andern an desselben stat kisen vnd welen in eime monade darnach al- lernehste, der si dunke vf ir eide als gelich vnd gemein, als der vor was. Ist aber das der tzweier egenanten rit- tern hr. Raben oder hr. Arnold einer abginge, so haben wir die egenanten Chunrad herre zu Winsperch vnd wir frowe Luckard sin elich wirtin vnd vnser lip erben vnd auch di egenanten vnser swager vnd swester, Greue Ru dolf von Wertheim vnd ouch Else sin elich wirtin vnd ir lip erben kraft vnd maht, ein andern zu setzen an des stat 81 der tode ist, itweder sit iglich teil, der in dartzu aller beste fugt vnd sullen des bedersit tun als dikke vnd als vil als des not geschiht on alle geuerde. Dise vorgeschriben rede alle geloben wir der egenante Chunrad herre zu Winsperch vnd auch wir egenant frowe Luckard vnd vnser lip erben für vns vnd alle vnser nachchomen, vff vnsere eide, den wir vorgenanter Chunrad von Winsperch darvber haben tzu den heilgen getan, war, stet vnd vnzerbrochen ewiclich tzu halten, vnd tzu eime waren vrkunde aller der vorge schriben rede geben wir dem vorgenanten vnserm swager, Greuen Rudolfen von Wertheim vnd auch vnserer swester frowe Elsen siner elichen wirtin der egenanten vnd ir lip erben disen offen brif, versigelten mit vnser beder insigel, di an disem brif sint gehangen, der ouch geben ist, als man zalt von Gotes geburt drutzehen hundert jar vnd in dem sibenden vnd tzwentzichsten jar an dem nehsten Montag vor Georij des heilgen. Lxxrv. Elisabeth von Hohenlohe, geborne Gräfin von Wert heim, stiftet durch einen Schenkungsbrief die Car- thause Grünau. 1328. März 16. In nomine domini amen. Nos Elyzabet filia quondam nobilis viri Bopponis comitis de Wertheym, rclicta quondam Gotfridi domini de Uohenloch, omnibus presentes literas inspecturis salutem in eo a quo omnis sapiencia derivatur. Quia juxta psalmistam, nisi dominus edificaverit domum, in vanum labo- rant, qui edificant: licet igitur dudum sollicite et interne ante retroacta tempora cogitare ceperimus ac devotis me- ditationibus diebus et noctibus involverimus mentem nostram, quomodo et qualiter regi regum domino de suis donis et he— neficiis nobis per eum impensis redderemus ad sui honoris gloriam et famulatus augmentum aliqualem recompensam, de- mum ex largiflua bonitate ipsius, sine qua nullum bonum concipitur et frequenti meditatione concepimus et in hoc fir— mavimus anchoram nostri cordis, quod felices essemus, si hujusmodi nostra sollicitudine expensisque ac oportunis labo- ribus humilem ordinem ac sanctam religionem fratrum Car- thusiens. quorum vita est exemplar vite et conversationis domini nostri Jesu Christi, dum in terris deguit humani ge- Wcrthein. tlrkundrnhui-h. r 82 neris pro salute ac sui precursoris clamantis in deserto, ad partes Franconie et Mogoni, ubi dictus ordo est incognitus, deducere valeremus. Quesita sic et inyenta oportunitate ut speramus dictis fratribus prope civitatem Mogunt. habitantibus nomine ipsorum et totius ordinis infrascripta bona juxta alveum Mogoni apud oppidum Wert heim dedimus, donavi- mus et damus in hiis scriptis. Et omiie jus et actionem no- bis competens in ipsis bonis directe vel indirecte in presenti vel in luturo, in dictos fratres et eorum ordinem transferi- mus per presentes, pure, simpliciter et in totum pro remedio animarum patris, matris, nostrorum progenitorum et consan- guineorum et nostrarum ac omnium et singulorum, qui ad hujusmodi donationem et translationem fideliter dederint au- xiiium, consilium vel favorem pro monasterio et conventu infra terminos dictorum bonorum in loco magis apto, qui ipsis placuerit construendo et deo perpetuo famulando, ut populus dei eorum sanctis eruditis exemplis in sue devotionis proficiat salubriter incrementis. Quam donationem et trans- lationem in vero verbo et bona fide promittimus ratam, gratam et firmam perpetue in omnibus tenere et etiam observare nee contravenire vel volenti consentire, verbo vel facto publice vel occulte, renunciantes libere, ex certa scientia omni so- lempnitate, si qua fieri consuevit vel deberet in donationibus vel Iranslationibus faciendis ac alio omni juris sufiragio ca nonici et civilis, per quod premissa vitiari possent, seu quo- modolibet impugnari. Et ad majorem certitudinem sponte eli- gentes, quod si aliquid contrarium faceremus ut premittitur in toto vel in parte, honorabiles viri et domini judices sancle Moguntin. seclis et ollicialis curie Herbipolens. vel alter eorum- dem reliquo minime requisito sententiam exeommunicationis in nos proferant usque ad dignam per nos satisfactionem omni judiciorum strepitu quiescente. Sunt autem hec bona, de quibus supra feeimus, videlicet: villa nostra Schalbrunnen cum suo districtu, marchia, hominibus, pratis, paseuis, agris, vineis, aquis, rivuKs, silvis, juribus, jurisdictionibus, redditi- bus, proventibus, spiritualibus et temporalibus, corporalibus vel incorporalibus ac aliis pertinentiis, attinentiis et depen- dentiis suis de alto et de basso uniyersis quoeunque nomine nuneupatis. entries.english:
The brothers Rudolf and Rudolf, Counts of Wertheim, purchase the village of Cellingen from Abbot Heinrich of Fulda. 16 March 1327.

“Henry, by the grace of God Abbot of the Church of Fulda,” makes known to all present and future that, with the unanimous, voluntary, and express consent of his beloved sons in Christ, Dean Theodoric and the entire chapter of his church, after due deliberation and careful discussion, he has sold and conveyed to the honorable and noble men Rudolf of Wertheim, canon of Würzburg’s principal church, and Rudolf, Count of Wertheim, brothers, for themselves and their heirs, the abbey’s village of Oellingen with all appurtenances belonging to him and his church there, whether known or yet to be discovered. The abbey’s lodgings are excepted and reserved for him and his successors. The price of 500 pounds of Hall silver has been paid in ready cash and applied to the manifest advantage of the abbot and his church; by this deed he freely grants and conveys the village by lawful sale. A condition is added: by special favor granted to the buyers, the abbot and his successors may redeem the village, with its rights and appurtenances, for the stated price of 500 pounds of Hall pennies in whatever year they wish, first from Rudolf the canon if he is then living, and otherwise from Rudolf the Count or his heirs. The redemption must be made within the fourteen days immediately before or after the Feast of the Chair of St Peter. Upon redemption, the village and all rights and appurtenances that had belonged to the abbot and his church will return freely and without hindrance to them; no person other than the abbot and his church may redeem it. The customary Roman-law security clauses in deeds of sale follow. The seals of the abbot and his convent, and also the dean and convent’s seal, are attached. Done and issued in the year of the Lord 1327, on the Monday after the Sunday on which Oculi is sung.

LXXIII. Agreement between Konrad, Lord of Weinsberg, and his lawful wife Luckard, née von Breuberg, and her brother-in-law Count Rudolf of Wertheim and his wife Else, née von Breuberg, concerning the future disposition of the former’s inheritance, especially the lordship of Breuberg. 20 April 1327.

We, Chunrad, Lord of Winsperch, and Lady Luckard, his lawful wife, née von Bruberch, publicly declare in this letter and make known to all who see or hear it that we have reached an agreement with the noble Count Rudolf of Wertheim, our brother-in-law, and Lady Else, his lawful wife, née von Bruberch, our natural sister, concerning all the property that has come or may yet come to the said Ladies Else and Luckard from our father and mother. With the advice of the honorable men named below—Sir Chunrad Schenk, Lord of Ertpach; Sir Raban von Helmstatt; and Sir Arnold von Rosenberg, knight—we have jointly chosen them as arbiters for all disputes or disagreements that may arise between us, our officials, castle retainers, servants, or other people concerning that inheritance and its property. They have settled the matter as follows.

If our beloved sister Lady Else of Wertheim should die without bodily heirs (which God forbid), our brother-in-law Count Rudolf of Wertheim shall peacefully hold and enjoy throughout his life all property and inheritance, whether known or unknown, that our sister Else received from her father and mother. Both before and after his death, all that property shall pass to us, Lady Luckard, and our bodily heirs, with the same rights our sister had until her death.

If we wish to sell all or part of the inheritance—whether castles, towns, villages, hamlets, bailiwicks, church patronages, fiefs, rents, revenues, woods, waters, pastures, or anything else belonging to it, whether known or unknown—we must first offer it openly to our brother-in-law Count Rudolf and our sister Lady Else, or, if she is no longer living, to her bodily heirs, two months in advance, so that they may buy it if they wish. The price they are to pay for the rents shall not exceed the following: ten pounds of pennies for each pound of annual cash rent; four pounds for each malter of annual grain rent; two pounds for each malter of annual oat rent; and, for each annual load of wine, the customary value in the region where the wine grows. If we, Lady Luckard, or our bodily heirs offer any of the said inheritance to Count Rudolf, Lady Else, or her bodily heirs at such a low price that they consider it too expensive, or do so deceitfully, we must submit the property to the three arbiters named above—Sir Chunrad Schenk, Sir Raban von Helmstatt, and Sir Arnold von Rosenberg. They shall assess it on oath, and we shall both abide by their decision under the oaths sworn by Chunrad of Winsperch and Count Rudolf to the saints.

If our brother-in-law Count Rudolf, our sister Lady Else, or her bodily heirs buy any part of the inheritance from Chunrad of Winsperch, Lady Luckard, or our heirs, they shall pay the purchase price in installments: one thousand pounds of pennies each quarter, more or less according to the purchase price, with interest and payments in proportion.

If Count Rudolf, Lady Else, or her heirs do not agree with us on the purchase within the two months after Chunrad and Luckard of Winsperch, or Luckard’s heirs, have duly offered it, then Chunrad, Luckard, and her heirs may sell or otherwise dispose of the property as they wish, wherever they can, and Rudolf, Else, and their heirs shall not obstruct them by word or deed to their detriment.

If any dispute arises between the officials, castle retainers, servants, or other people belonging to either side concerning the aforesaid inheritance, we shall not intervene ourselves. We have chosen Sir Chunrad Schenk of Ertpach, Sir Starkrad, and Sir Wortwin von Reibach, knights and castle retainers at Breuberg, to prevent and settle such quarrels within the month after they are reported. If the three cannot settle a matter in that month, they shall add the two knights named above, Sir Raban von Helmstatt and Sir Arnold von Rosenberg, and those five shall settle it amicably or according to law in the following month. If two of the three appointed knights agree, the third must accept their decision without objection. If one of the three dies, the other two shall choose a replacement within the next month. If Sir Chunrad Schenk dies, the two knights Raban von Helmstatt and Arnold von Rosenberg shall choose a suitable and impartial replacement on oath within the next month. If either of those two knights dies, both sides—the lord and lady of Winsperch and their heirs, and Count Rudolf, his wife Else, and their heirs—may each appoint whoever they consider most suitable in his place, as often as necessary.

We, the aforesaid Chunrad, Lord of Winsperch, Lady Luckard, and our heirs promise on our oaths, for ourselves and all our successors, to keep all these provisions true, firm, and unbroken forever. As true evidence, we issue this public letter to Count Rudolf of Wertheim, our brother-in-law, Lady Else, our sister and his lawful wife, and their heirs, sealed with both our seals. Issued in the year of the Lord 1327, on the Monday before St George’s Day.

LXXIV. Elisabeth von Hohenlohe, née Countess of Wertheim, founds the Charterhouse of Grünau by a deed of gift. 16 March 1328.

“In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Elyzabet, daughter of the late noble Boppo, Count of Wertheim, and widow of the late Gotfrid, Lord of Hohenlohe, greet all who see this letter in Him from whom all wisdom flows. The Psalmist says, ‘Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.’ For a long time we have diligently and inwardly considered, in devout meditation day and night, how we might make some return to the King of kings for His gifts and benefits, granted to us for His glory and the increase of His service. At last, through His abundant goodness, without which no good can be conceived, and by much reflection, we conceived this purpose and fixed our hearts upon it: we would be happy if, through our care, expense, and suitable labor, we could bring the humble order and holy religion of the Carthusian brothers—whose life is an example of the life and conduct of our Lord Jesus Christ when He dwelt on earth for the salvation of humankind, and of His forerunner crying in the wilderness—to Franconia and the region of the Main, where that order is unknown.

“Having sought and, as we hope, found a suitable opportunity, we give, have given, and by this deed donate, in the name of those brothers living near Mainz and of their entire order, the following properties beside the Main near the town of Wertheim. We transfer to those brothers and their order all right and claim we have in these properties, directly or indirectly, now or in the future, purely, simply, and wholly, for the salvation of the souls of our father, mother, ancestors, kin, ourselves, and everyone who faithfully gives aid, counsel, or support to this donation and transfer. The purpose is to build a monastery and convent within the boundaries of the said properties, at the place they prefer, and to serve God there perpetually, so that God’s people may grow in devotion through their holy and learned example.

“We promise in truth and good faith that this gift and transfer shall forever remain valid, approved, and firm in every respect, and that we shall observe it and neither act against it nor consent to anyone doing so, openly or secretly, by word or deed. We freely and knowingly waive every formality customarily required or that ought to be required for gifts or transfers, and every other remedy of canon or civil law by which the foregoing might be invalidated or challenged. For greater certainty, we voluntarily agree that if we act contrary to any part of this deed as stated above, the honorable judges of the Holy See of Mainz and the official of the Würzburg court, or either of them without requiring the other, may pronounce sentence of excommunication against us until we make due satisfaction, without further judicial proceedings.

“The properties are: our village of Schalbrunnen, with its district, boundary, people, meadows, pastures, fields, vineyards, waters, streams, woods, rights, jurisdictions, rents, revenues, spiritual and temporal assets, corporeal and incorporeal assets, and all other appurtenances and dependencies, whatever they may be called. Also two mills called ‘Yringes Mit ien,’ situated above the bank called ‘dye Hascia,’ upstream from Schalbrunnen. Also six acres of vines on the right-hand side when traveling from the Wertheim Cross toward Haselach, on the hill called ‘der Bylsteyn.’ Also, in the village of Altavil, twenty malters of rye and two malters of oats, reckoning two malters of oats as one malter of rye, payable by the feasts of St Michael and St Martin; and seven pounds of Hall pennies in annual rent there, payable every year on the Feast of St Martin, which we shall point out in person from our property if and when necessary. In witness of all these matters, our seal is attached to this deed. Done and issued in the year of the Lord 1328, on the Tuesday after the Sunday on which Laetare is sung.”
